stem: Find the next term in the series: 3, 6, 11, 18, 27, 38, ?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Adds 11 (same as the previous difference) to 38 instead of noting that differences increase by 2 each step.
Consecutive differences are 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 (odd numbers increasing by 2). Next difference = 13. Missing term = 38 + 13 = 51.
Identifies next difference as 13 but adds to 38 to get 51 then rounds up by 3 to 54 by a computational slip.
Assumes differences increase by 3 each step (3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 19...) and gets 38 + 19 = 57.

explanation: The differences between consecutive terms are 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 - odd numbers forming an AP with common difference 2. The next difference = 13. Answer = 38 + 13 = 51.

explanation_sections.punchline: Differences of 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 are consecutive odd numbers - the next must be 13.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: compute differences: 6-3=3, 11-6=5, 18-11=7, 27-18=9, 38-27=11. Differences are odd and increase by 2. Next difference = 13. Answer = 38 + 13 = 51.
explanation_sections.lesson: Odd-number differences (3, 5, 7, ...) generate a quadratic-looking series. Check second-level differences first.
explanation_sections.timing: 35-45 seconds. Once differences are listed as 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, the pattern is obvious. No trap in computation - just add 13 to 38.
